facts.claim: The plastisphere acts as a potential enrichment site for high-risk resistance genes.

facts.claim: Antibiotic resistance in the environment can be a mere reflection of the regional antibiotic resistance situation in the clinic.
facts.quote: In this Review, we present our current understanding of the roles of the environment, including antibiotic pollution, in resistance evolution, in transmission and as a mere reflection of the regional antibiotic resistance situation in the clinic.

facts.claim: Non-biodegradable polymers consistently demonstrated stronger enrichment than biodegradable ones in the plastisphere.
facts.quote: Non-biodegradable polymers consistently demonstrated stronger enrichment than biodegradable ones.

facts.claim: Antibiotic resistance genes are found in 50 samples from 10 typical environments, with 260 ARG subtypes belonging to 18 ARG types detected.
facts.quote: A metagenomic approach and network analysis was used to investigate the wide-spectrum profiles of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and their co-occurrence patterns in 50 samples from 10 typical environments. In total, 260 ARG subtypes belonging to 18 ARG types were detected

facts.claim: Environmental biofilms can be hotspots for the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes.
facts.quote: Several studies have demonstrated that environmental biofilms can be hotspots for the dissemination of ARGs.

facts.claim: The spread of vancomycin resistance genes in different environments is linked to the selective pressure resulting from vancomycin use.
facts.quote: The widespread occurrences and abundance variation trend of vancomycin resistance genes in different environments might imply the spread of vancomycin resistance genes because of the selective pressure resulting from vancomycin use.

research.angle: While antibiotic resistance genes are pervasive in environmental systems like biofilms and microplastics, the environment may sometimes simply reflect existing clinical resistance rather than acting independently.
research.verdict: The evidence confirms that antibiotic resistance genes are widespread in various environments and can be concentrated in specific niches like biofilms and microplastics.
research.caveat: It is unclear whether environmental resistance is an independent driver or merely a reflection of clinical antibiotic use.
